title: I’ve created a browser-based game that lets you experience the Apollo 17 lunar mission, but it feels a bit lacking in realism... How do you all handle this kind of thing?
author: Loud-Current1641
selftext:
I am currently developing a browser-based project that recreates the Apollo 17 mission (built using three.js; it’s free and requires no installation). The project covers the entire mission—from launch and lunar landing to the return to Earth. I’ve been working on the environment around the space center, the Earth’s atmosphere during launch, and the lunar surface, but I’m struggling to achieve a truly realistic look. I’m also aware that the textures for the Saturn V rocket and the spacesuits lack realism. (I often see incredibly realistic visuals in posts here on Reddit, and I’m curious—how do you all achieve that?)

Additionally, I’ve found that the "waiting periods"—such as during the transit to the Moon or the lead-up to the landing—can feel quite long. At the same time, I worry that cutting too much might compromise the sense of realism.

My goal is to keep the project as grounded in reality as possible, avoiding fictionalized elements.



For those with experience in creating simulations or documentaries, I have two questions:

1. Do you have any tips for achieving a realistic look for elements like the atmosphere, surface textures, and structures?

2. How can I shorten long, uneventful segments without losing the sense of scale or the vastness of the distances involved?



The project consists of nine chapters, spanning from launch to splashdown. You can check it out for yourself here: [https://junzzy827.github.io/solar-odyssey/](https://junzzy827.github.io/solar-odyssey/)

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/Loud-Current1641 please update this post with more on how you used AI to build the game. A line saying it was made with AI isn't enough. Share dev details. Rule 4 is there so promotional posts add to the sub by talking about the process and real development. We don't want the sub drowned in empty promotion. Posts that aren't updated may be removed.

replies.author: Loud-Current1641
replies.body: Thanks for the heads-up! I've added a section to the post on how it's made: directing Claude Code in Japanese across parallel feature threads, my role as playtester, real NASA audio with no AI-written lines, the script that checks the "8-second rule", a camera bug we hit while recording this clip, and where the AI-made visuals still fall short. Happy to go deeper on any of it.
